note: Written 5 Sep 2026 for Tranche 2. THE ATTRIBUTION ON THIS RECORD IS THE SURVEY'S AND IS NOT CORROBORATED HERE. The 1930s sheet says flatly 'Architect; Thomas Jefferson Builder: General John Hartwell Cocke (owner)'. No second source for the attribution was opened -- the Virginia DHR page for Bremo was not read -- so nothing in this corpus should harden the survey's line into a fact about who drew Bremo. What the record does establish cleanly is a two-storey brick house of about 1819 built by a member of Jefferson's own circle who lived on the estate while building it, which is why it is here. The survey states no dimension. Worth carrying for the node: the surveyor singles out 'its great stone barns and other outbuildings' as what makes the place notable, and the node's own prose is about a style whose dependencies are supposed to be buried.
